# Partial recursion for exact pattern-count distributions

**Setting.** Let $X_1,\dots,X_\ell$ be generated by an order-$m$ Markov source over a finite alphabet $\mathcal{A}$ (e.g. DNA or amino acids), and let $N_\ell$ count the occurrences of a pattern $\mathcal{W}$ (a regular language). A deterministic finite automaton for $\mathcal{A}^*\mathcal{W}$ with $R$ states turns the sequence into a homogeneous Markov chain on automaton states, and splitting its transition matrix into non-counting and counting parts, $\mathbf{P} + \mathbf{Q}$, gives the probability generating function

$$G_\ell(y) = \sum_{n\ge0}\mathbb{P}(N_\ell = n)y^n = \mathbf{u}\,(\mathbf{P} + y\mathbf{Q})^{\ell-m}\,\mathbf{v},$$

for a starting row vector $\mathbf{u}$ and the all-ones column vector $\mathbf{v}$.

**Partial recursion.** Assume $\mathbf{P}$ is irreducible, aperiodic and positive with Perron eigenvalue $\lambda$; put $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}} = \mathbf{P}/\lambda$, $\widetilde{\mathbf{Q}} = \mathbf{Q}/\lambda$, let $\nu$ be the modulus of the second eigenvalue of $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}$, and define $\mathbf F_k(i)=[y^k]\,(\widetilde{\mathbf P}+y\widetilde{\mathbf Q})^i\,\mathbf v$ (and $\mathbf F_k(i)=0$ for $i<0$) with iterated differences $\mathbf{D}^0_k(i) = \mathbf{F}_k(i)$, $\mathbf{D}^j_k(i) = \mathbf{D}^{j-1}_k(i) - \mathbf{D}^{j-1}_k(i-1)$. Then $\mathbf{D}^k_k(i) = \mathbf{C}_k + O(\nu^{i/(k+1)})$ for a constant vector $\mathbf{C}_k$, and for every $\alpha \ge 0$

$$\mathbb{P}(N_\ell = k) = \underbrace{\lambda^{\ell-m}\sum_{j'=0}^{k}\binom{\ell-m-\alpha-k+j'}{k}\mathbf{u}\,\mathbf{D}^{j'}_k(\alpha+j')}_{P_{k,\ell-m}(\alpha)} + \lambda^{\ell-m}\binom{\ell-m-\alpha}{k}O\big(\nu^{\alpha/(k+1)}\big).$$

So $P_{k,\ell-m}(\alpha)$ approximates $\mathbb{P}(N_\ell = k)$ with relative error $\frac{\lambda^{\ell-m}}{\mathbb{P}(N_\ell=k)}\binom{\ell-m-\alpha}{k}O(\nu^{\alpha/(k+1)})$.

## Expansion

The full recursion multiplies sparse matrices $\ell - m$ times, costing $O(\Omega n\ell)$ time for $\Omega = R|\mathcal{A}|$ nonzeros, and dyadic matrix powering ignores sparsity. The differences $\mathbf{D}^j_k$ obey the same sparse recursion $\mathbf{D}^j_k(i+1) = \widetilde{\mathbf{P}}\mathbf{D}^j_k(i) + \widetilde{\mathbf{Q}}\mathbf{D}^j_{k-1}(i)$, and the $k$-th difference becomes constant geometrically fast at the spectral-gap rate $\nu$, so the coefficient of $y^k$ is a polynomial of degree $k$ in $i$ up to an exponentially small error. Iterating only to $i \approx \alpha$, with $\alpha$ set by the desired precision and $\nu$, and extrapolating polynomially gives a cost independent of $\ell$ beyond $\alpha$. A second, complementary method expands an exactly reconstructed rational bivariate generating function $G(y,z) = \mathbf{u}(\mathbf{I} - z\mathbf{P} - yz\mathbf{Q})^{-1}\mathbf{v}z^m$; both are applied to transcription factor motifs on a human chromosome and PROSITE protein signatures.

## Sources

- Grégory Nuel and Jean-Guillaume Dumas, "Sparse approaches for the exact distribution of patterns in long state sequences generated by a Markov source", arXiv:1006.3246 (2010), Section 2 (Theorem 5, Corollary 6) and Section 3 (Lemmas 8-9, Proposition 10, Corollary 11), <https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1006.3246>.
